answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to forge a unique sequential hash chain starting from a public juniper root. Each step consumes non-parallelizable CPU time and must be attested by an unrelated established peer before the next step unlocks. Attackers spawning many clones pay the full sequential cost per head; a sudden cluster arriving like a comet triggers joint slash of their ferrous collateral, making bulk farming prohibitively expensive while one honest agent advances steadily.
